meta.purpose: Data Science and AI for Finance — a complete technical pathway plus eight buildable finance automation projects.
meta.principle: Build the manual process first, by hand. Automate only what you can already do correctly, because an automated error scales faster than a manual one.
meta.dataPolicy: Use synthetic, anonymised or public data only. Never put client, employer or personal data into a third-party model or a public repository.

automationProjects.title: Automated MIS Generator
automationProjects.problem: A finance team spends three days each month copying extracts into a report pack, and the copy-paste introduces errors.
approach: Validate the extract: required columns, control totals, period coverage
Map accounts to reporting lines from a maintained mapping table
Reconcile actuals to the trial balance
Compute actual, budget, variance and variance %
Generate the Excel pack with formatted sheets and charts
Write a run log and an exception list
automationProjects.deliverable: Python package or workbook + generated sample pack + README + validation log
evaluation: Reconciles to the trial balance exactly
Fails loudly on bad input rather than silently
Documented enough for another person to run
automationProjects.guardrail: Never overwrite the prior-month pack; archive every output with a timestamp.

automationProjects.title: Invoice Extraction System
automationProjects.problem: Vendor invoices arrive as PDFs and are keyed manually into the ERP, causing errors and duplicate payments.
inputs: A set of synthetic invoice PDFs in varied layouts
approach: Extract text and tables from the PDFs
Parse invoice number, date, vendor, GSTIN, line items, tax and total
Validate arithmetic: line totals sum to invoice total, tax computed correctly, GSTIN format valid
Match to purchase order and flag variances
Detect duplicates on vendor, invoice number, amount and date
Output a validated CSV plus an exception report
tools: Optional LLM for messy layouts with structured output
automationProjects.deliverable: Extraction pipeline + accuracy report + exception report + evaluation set
evaluation: Field-level accuracy measured on a labelled test set
Low-confidence items routed to human review
automationProjects.guardrail: A human must approve before any invoice is posted to the ledger. Extraction output is a draft, never a posting.

automationProjects.title: Expense Classification Assistant
automationProjects.problem: Employee expense claims are coded to the wrong GL accounts, distorting cost-centre reporting and GST credit.
inputs: Historical expense claims with descriptions, amounts, merchants and correct GL codes
approach: Clean and explore the history to find class balance
Establish a rule-based baseline using merchant and keyword mapping
Add a model or LLM classifier for the residual cases
Evaluate against a held-out set with per-class accuracy
Route low-confidence predictions to review
Report classification accuracy and cost per claim
automationProjects.deliverable: Classifier + confusion matrix + review queue design + policy note
automationProjects.guardrail: Never auto-approve an expense claim on model output alone.

automationProjects.title: Financial Statement Analyser
automationProjects.problem: Analysing each set of accounts takes hours of manual rekeying, and the arithmetic is easy to get wrong.
approach: Extract the primary statements
Normalise line items to a common schema
Verify that assets equal liabilities plus equity
Compute 20 ratios and a DuPont decomposition
Compare with prior years and peers
Generate a one-page analytical summary with limitations stated
tools: Optional LLM for narrative with strict grounding
automationProjects.deliverable: Analyser + validated output for three companies + methodology note
evaluation: Narrative makes no claim the data does not support
automationProjects.guardrail: Extraction must be reviewed against the source page before any number is relied on.

automationProjects.title: Tax Research Assistant
automationProjects.problem: Finding the applicable provision and its amendments takes time, and generic chatbot answers cannot be trusted.
inputs: A curated library of public tax material: Act text, rules, circulars, your own notes
A set of 30 research questions with verified answers
approach: Curate and chunk the source library with metadata: act, section, date, amendment status
Build retrieval over the library
Force citations to the retrieved source
Require the answer to state the date of the law relied on
Evaluate answer accuracy and citation correctness on the test set
Add an explicit 'verify before relying' instruction
evaluation: Unanswerable questions are refused rather than guessed
Evaluation set is independent of the prompt tuning
automationProjects.guardrail: Output is research support only. It is not tax advice, and every answer must be verified against the bare provision before use.

automationProjects.title: Budget Variance Explanation Tool
automationProjects.problem: Variance commentary is written under time pressure, tends to describe rather than explain, and often misses the real driver.
inputs: Actual vs budget data by cost centre and account
approach: Compute variances and rank by absolute and percentage significance
Decompose into volume, price, mix and rate effects where drivers exist
Draft commentary with the decomposition as evidence
Flag variances requiring investigation
Produce a review-ready draft with the numbers cited inline
tools: LLM for drafting with grounding in the computed numbers
automationProjects.deliverable: Tool + sample commentary pack + quality rubric
evaluation: Every statement is traceable to a computed figure
Root cause stated, not just the amount
Reviewer edits are minimal in a blind test
automationProjects.guardrail: The model drafts; the FP&A analyst owns and signs the commentary.

automationProjects.title: Accounting Question-Answering Assistant
automationProjects.problem: Students and staff repeatedly ask the same conceptual questions, and generic answers are inconsistent with the applicable framework.
inputs: Your own curated notes, standards summaries and worked examples
A test set of 50 questions with reference answers
approach: Structure the knowledge base with chapter and source metadata
Retrieve the most relevant chunks
Answer with a citation to the note and the standard
Distinguish AS from Ind AS where treatment differs
Evaluate on the test set with a rubric for accuracy and citation
Log unanswered questions to extend the library
tools: LLM API or a local model
automationProjects.deliverable: Assistant + test results + content gap log
automationProjects.guardrail: Never present an answer as examinable authority without naming the source and its edition.

automationProjects.title: Automated Reconciliation Prototype
automationProjects.problem: Bank, intercompany and vendor reconciliations consume days and still miss items.
inputs: Two synthetic data sets to reconcile, each with seeded exceptions: timing differences, duplicates, transposition errors, missing entries
approach: Normalise both sides: dates, amounts, references
Apply exact matching on amount and reference
Apply fuzzy matching on amount and date proximity
Classify unmatched items by probable cause
Produce a reconciliation statement and an ageing of unmatched items
Measure match rate and false-match rate
automationProjects.deliverable: Reconciler + reconciliation statement + exception analysis + accuracy metrics
evaluation: Separates true matches from false matches
Audit trail of every match decision
automationProjects.guardrail: Automated matches above a value threshold require human confirmation before adjustment.

capstone.name: Finance Automation Capstone
capstone.brief: Combine at least three of the eight projects into one governed workflow: ingest, validate, analyse, draft, human review, publish, log.
capstone.deliverable: Working system + architecture diagram + control matrix + evaluation report + AI use policy
capstone.evaluation: Technical accuracy (30%), control design (25%), evaluation evidence (20%), documentation (15%), professional judgement (10%)
